thesis:
One cumulative thesis runs through every brief since mid-September: the marginal dollar of human demand — and therefore of capital — is migrating from convenience to security, and from asset-light claims on the future to physical chokepoints that are hard to build. Households are buying guaranteed electrons, resilient supply, fraud protection, restored physical function, and above all reclaimed time; corporates are buying the same things in industrial form (behind-the-meter generation, sovereign/on-prem AI, cyber tooling, domestic materials processing). A ~5% risk-free rate with $365tn of global debt is the regime, not an anomaly, which means the discount rate permanently penalises business models whose moat was cheap capital (marginal housing, levered consumer, REIT roll-ups, second-tier AI capex) and rewards owners of cash-generative constraints.

The single most durable, repeatedly-restamped observation across all five briefs is that electricity — not GPUs — is the binding constraint on AI. Amazon's $8B Generac deal, Meta funding seven gas plants, Mitsui contracting LNG explicitly for data centres, Italy reversing a 40-year nuclear ban, Duke and Constellation guiding 2026 higher: energy and compute are converging into a single asset class. This is the highest-confidence multi-year channel we have (0.75–0.8 in the source claims) and it is the one place where narrative scores are very high (power-demand 85, grid 77, LNG 75) while pricing scores are low (34, 55, 56) — the market talks about it far more than it pays for it. The second most durable shift is that people buy AI as time, not intelligence: 'ai phone assistant', 'ai phone answering service', 'ai agent builder' are the fastest-rising consumer queries, and enterprises pay for measurable labour substitution while punishing per-seat pricing. That favours incumbents with distribution and workflow data (Microsoft, Intuit, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Palantir) and devices/silicon that run inference locally (Apple, Qualcomm, TXN), and makes the terminal value of pure centralized compute rental contestable even as near-term order books boom.

The third axis is bodily and financial self-defence. Health demand is bifurcating: pharmacological metabolic management on one side (Lilly gaining GLP-1 share), and procedures/devices on the other — the 107% surge in robotic-surgery queries spanning hysterectomy, hernia, prostate and knee is an ageing cohort shopping for restored function, which raises the bar for CGM franchises to prove incremental value. Financially, a demographic-scale need for advice, custody, fraud protection and multi-venue/multi-currency access is forming (aging parents, estate plans, scam clusters, tokenised 24/7 settlement, Texas Stock Exchange, Indian retail brokerage) — the intermediation layer wins whether the underlying assets do or not. Housing is the clearest example of a need that will NOT be resolved: 7.45% mortgages freeze turnover, behaviour adapts into repair-and-stay-put, smaller units, rental permanence and multigenerational households. That is bearish turnover-linked consumption and bullish MRO/renovation for years — and the attention data (LOW, HD, SHW, LEN all in the not-priced bucket) says the market hasn't marked it.

Positioning implication: own constraint owners and toll roads on power, memory, optics, copper, skilled trades and workflow data; be selective in the crowded, well-priced parts of AI (CRWD at 89 pricing, PANW 84, AMD 79 have negative gaps — the theme is right, the entry is not); and accept that the AI drawdown, when it comes, will be a financing event (circular vendor financing: Nvidia into Anthropic, vendor-linked cloud commitments) rather than a demand event — which means the physical suppliers with contracted backlogs survive it better than the equity-funded compute landlords.

theme_ranking.why: The most-repeated, highest-confidence claim across every brief: electrons are the binding constraint on AI. Narrative 85 vs pricing 34 and trend 31 is the widest talk-vs-pay gap in the graph — the market narrates it daily and pays for almost none of it. Demand is contracted (Meta gas plants, Mitsui LNG, Amazon generators) not speculative.

Transmission, interconnect, switchgear and EPC are the physical bottleneck behind the power thesis, with a decade-long capex runway and skilled-trade scarcity protecting contractor margins. Narrative 77 vs pricing 55 still leaves room; Quanta/Comfort Systems raised outlooks are evidence, not hope.

Demand is real and self-funding at hyperscaler level, but attention 83 vs pricing 57 with circular vendor financing means the payoff is concentrated in the physical links — memory, optics, networking — rather than in compute landlords. Own the constraint (MU, AVGO, CIEN, CRDO), not the balance-sheet exposure.

Structurally the most non-discretionary budget line in the stack: AI supercharges scams, enterprise data-sovereignty fears push spend on-prem, and one breach broke a medtech's guidance. High conviction on the theme, poor entry — pricing 75 with CRWD at 89 and PANW at 84 means the truth is fully paid for; prefer ZS/FTNT-type entries.

Highest trend score (71) with pricing only 52. People buy AI as time, not intelligence, and enterprises pay for measurable labour substitution. The winners are distribution/workflow incumbents (MSFT, INTU, CRM, NOW, PLTR); the losers are seat-priced tools that can't show substitution.

Gas is the marginal AI fuel for the next three years and LNG is being contracted explicitly for data centres. Energy security is now a financial variable ($107 crude, export-ban politics). Narrative 75 vs pricing 56 with cash-generative producers at 5% discount rates.

Trend 66 with pricing 55 and modest narrative 49 — the quiet way to own sovereignty capex (Micron Sanand, Nvidia-Australia) plus the edge-inference wave. China's Ascend 960 caps Western accelerator TAM but raises domestic-fab and test intensity everywhere else.

Strongest consumer-behaviour signal in the dataset (attention 82, the fastest-rising query set), and the cost/latency/privacy logic is structural. But narrative 73 and pricing 59 mean part of it is already paid for; the durable capture is in device silicon and handset/OS owners, not in app-layer assistants.

Supply-chain sovereignty, not tariffs, is the long war, and rare-earth leverage confirms it. Low narrative (40) and modest attention (36) despite a multi-decade spend — the skilled-trades and mechanical-contracting layer is where the cash actually lands.

Durable utility demand and the labour market is voting for it ('cloud computing salary/certification' +53%), but attention 72 and pricing 61 mean it is well understood. Growth persists; excess return does not.

Italy reversing a 40-year ban plus explicit US policy support for AI-driven nuclear gives multi-year order books for reactors, fuel and interconnection. Trend 35 and pricing 36 against narrative 59 means it is cheap optionality — but the horizon is genuinely 5-20 years and interim cash flows are thin.

A 107% surge in robotic-surgery intent with granular procedure-level queries, against pricing 40 and trend 39, is the clearest unpriced demographic demand signal in the set. People want restored function; they are researching the machine before the surgeon.

24/7 tokenised settlement, multi-venue fragmentation and a demographic-scale need for advice, custody and fraud protection make the intermediation layer a winner regardless of asset returns. Pricing 54 already reflects some of it (IBKR at 72).

Physically required by every part of the power and data-centre thesis, but pricing 62 already discounts a lot and industrial flows are currently negative. Supply-constrained repricing is a when, not an if — the timing is the risk.

Direct expression of the status-migrates-to-scarce-physical-things shift and of $365tn of sovereign debt. Balanced scores (trend 47 / pricing 49) make it a portfolio hedge rather than an alpha source.

Real transition from demo to procurement (5,000 Optimus units, robot controllers, autonomous freight), but pricing 61 and narrative 72 versus trend 48 say expectations run ahead of unit economics — the Tesla Semi non-reaction is the market telling you it now wants numbers.

Security as a standing consumption category for states (NATO warnings, drone strikes on critical infrastructure), and pricing 41 is undemanding — but trend 40 shows the order-book conversion is slow and politically lumpy.
Trend 58 confirms real behavioural adoption, but pricing 67 means the easy money is gone and the category is now a share war (Lilly vs Novo) rather than a TAM expansion.

The underlying need is the most unmet in the dataset, but the investable expression is wrong-footed for years: 7.45% mortgages, price cuts, frozen turnover. The demand is real; the profit migrates to renovation/MRO, not builders. Trend 22 / narrative 13 is an accurate read, not a mispricing.

Fleet economics are turning (record diesel, $5,851/yr ownership cost, 'why buying trucks stops making sense'), and freight autonomy is scaling — but pricing 58 against a 3-10 year horizon means patience is required and the capital intensity is brutal.

Behaviourally correct and recurring (fuel back in the budget, trading down, Walmart guidance up) but narrative 77 vs trend 34 means it is a crowded macro story with a 1-5 year shelf life that ends when energy prices normalise.

The agent-owns-the-transaction-layer shift is the largest re-plumbing of ad economics since mobile, but it is explicitly labelled speculative, attention is only 25, and the outcome (who holds intent) is genuinely uncertain. High payoff, low resolution.

Real demographic pull, but pricing 61 versus attention 33 and the 09-25 observation that behaviour is bifurcating toward pharmacology raises the bar for continuous-monitoring franchises to prove incremental value.
Orbital compute and sovereign comms are live ideas (SpaceX/Nvidia), but the 5-20 year horizon and narrative 60 vs trend 60 make it a story that consumes capital at a 5% discount rate for a long time.

Globalisation around Asian rails and agent-initiated transactions are real, but the next billion financial relationships form outside US platforms — that is a headwind, not a tailwind, for the incumbent names in this universe. Trend 38 confirms.
The home-consolidation of entertainment is durable and evidenced (Visa card data), but it is a share shift inside a mature, ad-cyclical wallet with trend 48 and pricing 40 — modest structural alpha.

Convenience delegation continues and fuel costs push delivery aggregation over personal trips, but trend 33 and pricing 50 say the economics are competed away; it is infrastructure for someone else's margin.

Demand is being rationed by fuel cost, not desire — which is exactly the setup where operators cannot monetise the want (Ryanair capacity cuts, NCLH guidance cut). Narrative 23 is honest; the structural squeeze persists while crude is elevated.

Trend 24 is the weakest in the graph while pricing sits at 52. The tokenisation-of-settlement thesis is real but its beneficiaries are scaled brokers and custodians, not the tokens; exchange hacks reinforce the security tax.

beneficiary_profiles: Constraint owners of electrons: independent power producers, regulated utilities with data-centre interconnect queues, behind-the-meter generation and gas turbine/switchgear suppliers — they sell the one input that cannot be substituted or compressed.

Skilled-trade toll roads: mechanical/electrical contractors and transmission EPC with multi-year backlogs and pricing power from labour scarcity (FIX, PWR-type). Margin comes from the shortage of people who can install, not from technology.

Picks-and-shovels of the AI physical layer: memory, optics, interconnect, test and EDA — consumed by inference and edge deployment regardless of training cadence, and least exposed to a financing-driven capex pause.

Workflow-and-distribution incumbents in software: owners of enterprise data and the seat relationship that can convert agents into measurable labour substitution, rather than model vendors or seat-priced point tools.
Device and OS owners capturing migrating inference margin as compute moves to the edge for cost, latency and privacy.
Non-discretionary security taxes: cyber platforms, identity and fraud protection — spend that rises with AI adoption and with scam sophistication, and is expensed before growth budgets.
Repair-and-stay-put beneficiaries: home improvement retail, coatings, MRO, HVAC replacement — the profit pool created when housing turnover freezes rather than resolves.
Procedure-and-device healthcare: less-invasive surgical platforms and implantables serving an ageing cohort that shops for restored function.
Scaled intermediaries of money: brokers, custodians and advice platforms that monetise 24/7, multi-venue, multi-currency access and the demographic wave of estate/retirement complexity.
Cash-generative hard-asset owners: low-cost energy producers, copper, gold — the equity forms that survive a permanently elevated term premium.
Avoid: businesses whose moat was cheap capital — marginal homebuilders, levered consumer lenders, REIT roll-ups, equity-funded compute landlords and re-leveraging experience operators.

not_priced_candidates.why: Attention +72% and flagged not-priced. Direct expression of the highest-confidence behavioural substitution in the dataset: 7.45% mortgage lock-in converts moving into improving. The market is marking the housing freeze as bad for everything housing-linked, when it is unambiguously good for renovation and MRO volume.

Attention +51% then +59% across two briefs, still in the not-priced bucket, and already beating on results. Repair-and-stay-put is a multi-year behaviour, not a quarter, and HD also captures the professional contractor channel that benefits from the same skilled-trade scarcity driving the capex theme.

In the attention-not-priced list with opportunity 67 and gap 21 at pricing 48. Gas as the marginal AI fuel plus $107 crude plus a 5% discount rate that rewards cash return over growth — energy and compute converging into one asset class is not reflected in a 48 pricing score.

Gap 17, pricing 47, flagged not-priced. Optics is the least-discussed of the physical AI chokepoints (memory gets the headlines) yet data-centre interconnect and DCI scale with every megawatt deployed. Exposure to the buildout without the accelerator-cycle concentration risk.

Opportunity 74 with gap 29 at pricing 54 — the widest quality-adjusted gap among the physical AI names. Memory is the tightest link and the least exposed to a frontier-training pause because edge and inference consume HBM/DRAM regardless of cadence. Pricing 54 does not reflect a structurally tight cycle plus sovereign-fab tailwinds.

Pricing 19 with gap 34 and opportunity 54, mapped to the theme with the largest narrative-vs-pricing divergence in the graph (power-demand: narrative 85, pricing 34). Whatever one thinks of subsidy politics, the market is paying almost nothing for the megawatt-supply side of the AI power crunch.

Pricing 13 with gap 35 — the cheapest expression of a theme the system rates as a live structural question (who owns intent when agents transact). Deeply out of favour, which is exactly when an optionality-rich position on the re-plumbing of ad economics is worth owning.

Opportunity 74 with gap 47 at pricing 24 and on the not-priced list — the largest gap in the entire universe. Agentic ad targeting is a real, measurable labour/ROAS substitution, and the market is pricing it as a discredited story rather than a cash machine.

Opportunity 68, gap 30, pricing 25. The clearest owner of the 'agents that DO things' thesis in SMB workflow: it holds the financial data, the distribution and the pricing power to charge for outcomes rather than seats — precisely the model the 09-13 observation says wins while seat-priced software gets punished.

Gap 28 at pricing 35 despite being the most exposed of the large caps to contracted compute and sovereign/on-prem AI deployment — the exact channel the 09-14 enterprise-data-fear claim says accelerates. Financing-structure scepticism has overshot into the price.

Gap 21 at pricing 38 with no assigned theme — a blind spot. Chinese silicon sovereignty, sovereign fabs and edge-inference proliferation all raise design starts; EDA is a toll road on every one of them and is being priced as a cyclical semi.

On the not-priced list, and Buffett bought 10% the day after a guidance cut. The housing shortage stays a pricing problem through the late 2020s; scale builders with land and balance sheet are the survivors that consolidate share from marginal builders killed by the 5% regime. Painful entry, structurally correct.
Flagged not-priced and the purest margin expression of repair-and-stay-put: coatings volume tracks renovation and maintenance, not turnover, and it carries pricing power through a high-rate regime.

Named in two separate multi-year claims (09-14, 09-24) as the beneficiary of dedicated gas generation for data centres, with gap 14 at pricing 41. The contracting behaviour — Meta funding seven plants, Mitsui buying LNG for DCs — is observed fact, not forecast.

Named in both power-procurement claims with gap 14. Mechanical contracting is the skilled-labour chokepoint the 09-24 brief identifies as the real bottleneck to AI, reshoring and grid capex; backlog and wage-premium pass-through are durable, and pricing 53 treats it as an ordinary industrial.

Gap 23 at pricing 18 with no assigned theme. Edge inference and always-on agents raise the value of the connectivity layer, and in a 5% world a cash-generative, low-churn subscription utility is exactly the kind of short-duration compounder the term-premium claim favours.

anti_theses: 'Consumer humanoid robots are a 3-year market.' The order book is real (5,000 Optimus units, robot controllers) but the 09-13 brief is explicit that construction robotics won't cut housebuilding labour cost this cycle, and the 09-25 Tesla Semi non-reaction shows the market now demands unit economics. Robotics pricing at 61 vs trend 48 means you are paying for adoption that arrives after 2030.

'The housing shortage will be resolved by building more.' Every brief says the opposite: builders cut price rather than volume, contract signings -4.7%, prefab factories pivoting, demand migrating to smaller/manufactured/rented formats. The need is permanent; the supply response is not coming at 7.45% mortgages. Betting on a volume recovery is the wrong expression of a correct observation.

'China AI demand comes back as optionality for Western accelerators.' Huawei's Ascend 960 on a Q1 2027 timetable means the correct model is structurally zero, not a recovery call. Any NVDA/AMD thesis that carries China revenue as upside is double-counting.

'Rates revert to 3% and long-duration growth re-rates.' $365tn of global debt, a 5.44% 30-year and governments competing with corporates at every auction make elevated term premium the regime. The popular 'just wait for cuts' positioning is the single most consensus and least evidenced long-term idea in the set.

'Cybersecurity is under-owned.' The theme is right — non-discretionary, strengthening — but pricing 75, CRWD at 89 and PANW at 84 with negative gaps mean the insight is fully capitalised. Being right about the theme and wrong about the entry is the most common error this quarter.

'CGM and continuous monitoring are the default infrastructure of metabolic health.' The 09-13 brief asserted this; the 09-25 brief contradicted it — behaviour is bifurcating toward pharmacological management, raising the bar for device franchises to prove incremental value. Treat the earlier observation as superseded.

'Crypto is the hedge against sovereign debt debasement.' Trend 24 is the weakest score in the graph while pricing sits at 52, and the actual observed security-seeking behaviour went to gold, nuclear and physical assets (South Korean retail dumping semi ETFs for gold), not tokens. The real tokenisation winners are the custodians and brokers.

'Neoclouds and pure compute landlords are the way to own AI.' Demand is real but the financing is circular (Nvidia into Anthropic, vendor-linked cloud commitments), and the 09-25 brief flags the terminal value of centralized GPU rental as contestable once inference migrates to the edge. The drawdown will be a capital-structure event and the landlords are the levered leg.

'Travel and experiences are a durable post-pandemic structural growth story.' Demand is being rationed by fuel cost, capacity is being cut (Ryanair), and guidance is falling (NCLH). People still want the experience; the operator cannot sell it profitably at $107 crude. Narrative 23 is the market already conceding this.

'E-commerce convenience is still a margin-expanding structural theme.' Trend 33 with pricing 50 says the convenience delegation is real but fully competed; the value is migrating to whoever owns the agent and the intent, not to the fulfilment network.
what_would_change: Electricity prices or data-centre interconnect queues easing materially — if power stops being the binding constraint (new generation comes online faster than compute demand, or AI capex guidance is cut), the entire power/grid/LNG ranking drops by two tiers.

A visible AI financing accident: a failed neocloud refinancing, a hyperscaler cutting capex guidance, or the circular vendor financing (Nvidia-Anthropic-style) unwinding publicly. That would confirm the drawdown-as-financing-event thesis and argue for rotating from equipment/backlog names into contracted utilities and cash.

The 10-year sustainably below ~3.5% with mortgage rates in the 5s. That breaks the repair-and-stay-put trade (LOW/HD/SHW), revives turnover-linked consumption and homebuilders, and partially rehabilitates the cheap-capital business models we currently call impaired.

Agent monetisation proving out or failing: if a major platform demonstrates agent-initiated transaction take rates at scale, advertising-attention and ai-software-agents jump sharply; if agents stay demos through 2027, the time-delegation shift is real in search data but unmonetisable and the theme deflates.

Edge inference share data: if on-device inference captures a meaningful fraction of token volume within 18 months, rotate margin expectation from compute landlords toward device silicon (AAPL, QCOM, TXN); if it stalls, centralized cloud pricing power is more durable than we assume.
Crude and diesel normalising below ~$70 — that unwinds the value-retail rotation, revives travel/experiences and mid-tier dining, and weakens the energy-as-security consumption argument.
Memory pricing rolling over or a large HBM capacity addition landing early — that removes the tightest-link argument and de-rates MU/optics as defensive AI exposure.

Robotic-surgery search intent converting into procedure volume and device revenue in reported numbers (or not) over the next 2-3 quarters — the single cleanest test of whether the 107% query surge is a real unpriced demand signal or noise.

Credit stress migrating from search behaviour ('second-chance car loans', duration stretching) into delinquency data — that would accelerate the consumer bifurcation and argue for defensive staples and value retail over anything discretionary or financing-dependent.

A US policy reversal on nuclear licensing or a Western reactor cost overrun scandal — either would sharply re-rate the nuclear theme in one direction or the other from its current cheap-optionality state.

Evidence on GLP-1 versus device-and-discipline: if metabolic pharmacology continues taking share from monitoring franchises, further de-rate longevity/CGM exposure; if real-world adherence data favours combined device management, reverse it.
